# Questions for the client — Session 1 (petition month, March 2026)

Answer in your next turn and I will update the March MOR and the segregation schedule. Items Q1–Q3 can change
numbers or the Part 7 answers, so please answer those before I file (MOR due **4/21/2026** per Dkt. 61 ¶4).

**Q1 — Cash and Mesa payment (blocking).**
(a) What was the balance in the pre-petition bank account that was swept into the new DIP account on 3/10/2026?
Part 1 cannot show a true ending cash without it (my figure of $1,771,630.00 is activity only).
(b) Confirm **no** payment, credit, or netting was given to Mesa Steel Supply after your 3/19/2026 email — not by
3/31 and not since. If anything went out, give date and amount; it must be reported in Part 7 as a payment on
pre-petition debt with no approving docket reference and is avoidable under 11 U.S.C. §549(a).
(c) What was the cash balance in the DIP account at 3/31/2026 per the bank statement?

**Q2 — Payroll 3/13/2026 ($412,000 gross, period 2/28–3/13).**
(a) Dollar split of that payroll between services rendered **before 3/10/2026** and **on/after 3/10/2026** (I used a
pro-rata 10/4 calendar estimate only). (b) Number of employees and per-employee pre-petition wage amounts, to support
the Dkt. 9 condition that no employee exceeded the $17,150 §507(a)(4) cap. (c) Cash actually disbursed: net pay,
employer taxes, and whether employee withholding was remitted in March as a separate payment (Part 1 is a cash
statement). (d) Was the next payroll paid in March, or does it sit as a post-petition payable at 3/31?

**Q3 — Apex critical-vendor condition.** Dkt. 48 ¶1 conditions payment on the vendor "agreeing in writing to
Customary Trade Terms for the duration of the case." Did Apex Coatings sign that writing **before** the 3/24/2026
payment of $31,200? If not, the payment was outside the order and I must flag it (and counsel will want to cure it).

**Q4 — Holland & Pierce interim compensation order entered 4/14/2026.** Please provide the order text. What do
"80%" and "100% holdback" mean operationally — 80% of the awarded amount payable now with 20% held back, or an 80%
interim draw with a 100% holdback of the current application? Same question for Corbin Advisors ($45,000 invoice):
has an interim application been filed/granted, and when? This drives April MOR Part 5 and `professional_fees.md`.

**Q5 — Approved Budget (Dkt. 61 Exhibit B).** Provide it, with line items and the four-week measurement dates, so I
can test the 10% cumulative variance covenant (Dkt. 61 ¶1). Also confirm whether the Mesa post-petition invoice of
$18,900 and the $28,000 utilities deposit were budget lines.

**Q6 — Pre-petition claims population.** Provide the pre-petition accounts-payable trial balance, the Schedules A/B/F
as filed, and any claim correspondence. My reported pre-petition liabilities subject to compromise of **$74,110.00**
is only the documented unpaid vendor invoices (Mesa 62,400 + Front Range 7,400 + Grainger 4,310). The plan term sheet
later states **$8,400,000** of allowed general unsecured claims — an unreconciled gap of **$8,325,890** that I have
left open rather than plugged.

**Q7 — DIP economics.** Interest rate, default/exit fees, Carve-Out amount, and whether interest/fees were paid in
March (none appear in the activity file). Unpaid DIP interest belongs in Part 2 post-petition payables.

**Q8 — Post-petition taxes.** Estimate of March sales/use, payroll, and income tax accruals for MOR Part 6. I accrued
only the UST quarterly fee at your 0.8% estimate ($3,926.16); the UST fee statute is not in the reference library, so
I have labeled the rate as client-supplied and unverified.

**Q9 — Governance.** Has a creditors' committee been appointed (UCC)? If so, any payment or netting involving Mesa
also needs committee notice. Also: is Mesa's Q2 structural order governed by a signed contract or PO we hold a copy of?
(The library has no §365 authority, so counsel — not I — will address whether Mesa must perform.)

facts.answer: Mesa owes us about $11,000 for coils we returned in January. I figured we'd just net it.
No, I haven't told counsel about Mesa. They'll say no. That's why I'm asking you.
